summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, and recent SVC repair presented with fever, chills, and right-sided chest pain. She was found to have a superficial thrombus in the right basilic vein and evidence of right upper lobe pneumonia on imaging. She was treated with IV antibiotics, which were later transitioned to oral levofloxacin, and continued on fondaparinux for HIT. Her fever resolved within 48 hours, and she improved clinically. A PICC line could not be placed due to extensive venous occlusive disease. She was discharged home in stable condition with a plan for outpatient antibiotic completion and follow-up.
